I have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years, and I finished high school, so I don't just follow the crowd. I keep a small notebook where I write down what I spend and what I get back every year. Our soil here is loamy alluvial land, but after pulling wheat and maize off it for decades, the potassium is running thin and I have to put it back. I also stop at the seed dealer in town to compare varieties, and I ask my neighbors what worked before I decide.

I split my land into two blocks. Six mu are in the wheat-maize rotation, and three mu are cotton. The wheat went into the ground last October — I sowed Jimai 22, an improved variety, at 13 kg per mu, and I rotary tilled the field before sowing. Now it is early spring and the wheat is greening up. For this wheat crop, I will apply 32 kg of pure nitrogen per mu in total. That comes from 40 kg of urea that I split in two — half at green-up and half at jointing — plus 100 kg of compound fertilizer I put down as basal. Through that compound I also get 20 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times from my well: green-up water, jointing water, and one at heading. I will spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once if I see powdery mildew. If the weather holds, I expect 1000 kg per mu.

Right after I harvest the wheat in mid-June, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize on the same six mu. I will not plough — I no-till straight into the wheat stubble because every day delayed after June 15 costs me yield. I broadcast 90 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, the 28-6-6 type, which gives me about 23 kg of pure nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 7 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once if it is dry around the seven-leaf stage, and once absolutely at tasseling and silking — that second irrigation decides the yield. Two sprays for corn borer and aphids. I am targeting 1100 kg per mu.

My other three mu are cotton. I rotary till in late April and plant a hybrid variety. Cotton needs more potassium than grain crops, so I apply 100 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer, which works out to about 16 kg of pure nitrogen, 15 kg of phosphorus, and 15 kg of potassium per mu. I also topdress 15 kg of urea at flowering. I irrigate twice, at flowering and at peak boll. The hard part is spraying — I will spray 13 times from June to August for aphids, bollworm, and spider mites. At 70 years old, getting on the sprayer that many times is not easy, but cotton pays if you protect it. I expect 550 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer prices went up again this year, but I ran the numbers in my notebook. Cutting nitrogen by 5 kg per mu saves maybe 15 yuan, but on my 6 mu of wheat that risks losing 50 kg of grain per mu. At 2.4 yuan per kg, that is 120 yuan per mu lost — eight times what I save. I would rather spend the money and sleep well. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost.
